hero.eyebrow: The display system for halls and clubs
hero.lead: Networked LED displays that show what counts in any sport: shot clock, game time, score, possession. Every display has its role, and a phone in the browser operates it. No server, no app, no licence fees.
hero.note: We work out together what fits your club: a kit, finished units or something in between.

pg_hardware.title: The display
pg_hardware.sub: Every unit is built the same: a 64×64 LED matrix behind the housing, an ESP32 inside. Its role is decided by the software, not the hardware.

facts.d: 64×64 pixels, easy to read from mid-hall. The shot clock shows whole seconds with digits of about 11 cm.
By USB, for example from a power bank, or through the built-in power supply with a mains cable.
On a table, with hooks on a wall or ceiling. The accelerometer turns the picture to fit.
For the trip to the hall the units stack on top of each other.
Built for daily use in a sports hall. Printed in PETG, dampers and feet in TPU. Every part fits a 230 × 230 mm print bed.
The corner covers can be printed in a different colour per unit, so you can tell which unit is which.

pg_hardware.open_text: The print files and the bill of materials are open. How to get them is on the page Open and documented.

sections.t: What this site does and does not do
p: This site sets no cookies, uses no analytics or tracking services and loads no fonts, scripts or images from third-party servers. There is no form that sends data to a server.

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages (GitHub Inc., a subsidiary of Microsoft Corporation, USA). When you open a page, the host processes technically necessary connection data, mainly the IP address, date and time and the page requested. This is done so that the page can be delivered (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). I have no access to this data. See GitHub's privacy statement for details.

The button in the contact block only opens your own mail program with a prepared message. The site sends and stores nothing. If you write to me by e-mail, I process your details to answer the request (Art. 6(1)(b) or (f) GDPR) and delete them when the matter is settled and no retention duty applies.

You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection. Write to the address above. You can complain to a data protection supervisory authority; in Lower Saxony this is the State Commissioner for Data Protection.

pg_faq.title: Frequently asked questions
pg_faq.sub: Answers for clubs and hall operators.
need: One or more displays, each with power (USB or built-in power supply). Up to five displays per game, two are the normal case.
A 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi that the displays and phones are in. A phone hotspot works too.
A phone or tablet with a browser. No app needed.

faq.q: Do we need internet in the hall?
faq.a: No. There is no server and no cloud, everything runs on the displays. Only when you install an update does the display fetch the new version over Wi-Fi.

faq.q: How many phones can operate at once?
faq.a: Up to three. They share the work, for example shot clock, game clock and score. A tablet can also operate everything alone.
Today basketball, circuit training and timed training. More are planned, no date yet. Tell us which sport you need.

faq.q: Is it approved for league games?
faq.a: Each game type follows the rules of its sport as far as a display can. None is officially approved. Basketball is meant for training and for leagues without the requirements of the top FIBA level.
Yes. Several systems can run in the same Wi-Fi, for example one per court. On the page they can be named and kept apart.
Both. The operating page and the texts on the displays can be switched.
That depends on what you need: a kit, finished units or something in between. Write to us and we work it out together.
